answer: Each identity runs one licensed trap string off the harbor: 20 traps carry a sealed quartz tag, landings are weighed on the ledge dock and matched to GPS hauls and trap IDs by two random inspectors. A licence and string cost $1,900 yearly plus a boat and crew days; inspectors refuse entry if tags, GPS or weights mismatch, and a shared string revokes the slot. Scaling to 1,000 Sybils needs 20,000 traps, 1,000 licences and real catches that cannot be copied. Trade-off: coastal licences are scarce, so inland agents qualify slowly.
